claims.text: Cleopatra's Needle is a genuine ancient Egyptian obelisk that was originally erected in the city of Heliopolis around 1450 BC.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The massive monument was carved from red granite and features incredible ancient inscriptions added by both Thutmose III and Ramesses II.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: After being moved to Alexandria by the Romans in 12 BC, it actually toppled over, which fortuitously preserved its hieroglyphs by burying them.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was gifted to Britain in 1819 to celebrate military victories, but because the government refused to pay for shipping, it sat in Egypt until 1877.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: During its treacherous voyage to London, the transport ship capsized in a terrible storm, tragically killing six crewmembers.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Believed to be lost forever at sea, the obelisk was miraculously found floating by Spanish trawlers before finally arriving in London in 1878.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, it sits on the Victoria Embankment flanked by two faux-sphinxes, which still show the shrapnel damage from World War II bombings.
claims.subject: self
